title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is the Kummer-line description of the Legendre-type family. Over a base S with residue characteristics ≠ 2, take P^1_S with the three marked points J = {0,1,∞} and a fourth section t. Here t is the image of the origin of an elliptic curve E_0 under the degree-2 quotient p: E_0 → Σ_J ≅ E_0/{1,σ}, where σ = −1. The points 0, 1, ∞ are the images of the three nonzero 2-torsion points.

Previous page. Grothendieck wrote down the three involutions σ_j^t. Each is induced by translation by a 2-torsion point. Their fixed-point divisors Δ_j^t are the images of the points P with 2P = j, that is, the primitive 4-torsion lying over the 2-torsion point j:
- Δ_0: z² − 2z + t = 0
- Δ_1: z² = t
- Δ_∞: z² − 2tz + t = 0

Multiplication by 2 on E_0 descends to a degree-4 self-map f_2^t of P^1 (a Lattès map). It sends Δ_j to j with multiplicity 2, and sends 0, 1, ∞, t to t. Hence f_2^t = c_t·((z²−2z+t)/(z²−2tz+t))². Evaluating at ζ with ζ² = t gives c_t = t.

This page.
- (37) records f_2^t(z) = t·((z²−2z+t)/(z²−2tz+t))².
- It checks that f_2^t sends 0, 1, ∞, t to t, i.e. that the inner ratio is ±1 at these points. At z = t the ratio is (t²−t)/(t−t²) = −1.
- NB: the n-th iterate (f_2^t)^{∘n} = f_{2^n}^t is the map induced by 2^n·id_{E_0} on the quotient. The inverse image of the section t under f_{2^n}^t is the image p(E_0[2^n]) of the subgroup scheme of 2^n-torsion points.

Purpose. This gives an explicit coordinate description of the 4-torsion (and 2^n-torsion) of the Legendre-type family on the Kummer line. It is used immediately afterwards (§4 on the next page) to determine the moduli of elliptic curves with level-4 structure, M_11(4), via the extension 0 → E[2] → E[4] → E[2] → 0 and torsors under End(E[2]).
errors: Minor slip in the verification: at z = 1 the ratio (z²−2z+t)/(z²−2tz+t) equals (t−1)/(1−t) = −1, not 1. Only z = 0 and z = ∞ give +1; z = 1 and z = t give −1. This is harmless because the ratio is squared, so f_2^t(1) = t still holds.

The verification only checks the four 2-torsion images. That each Δ_j maps to j is built into the construction, so the formula is correct. Independent check: with ζ² = t the ratio equals −ζ/t, its square is 1/t, hence c_t = t.

ideas.what: Explicit degree-4 map on P^1 induced by multiplication by 2 on a Legendre-type elliptic curve, normalized so that the 2-torsion images are 0, 1, ∞ and the origin image is t
ideas.modern_name: Lattès map / duplication formula on the Kummer line (x-coordinate doubling)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weierstrass/Legendre duplication formulas; Lattès 1918 for dynamics)

ideas.what: Fixed loci of the translation-by-2-torsion involutions on the Kummer line identified with images of 4-torsion points halving a given 2-torsion point
ideas.modern_name: Kummer-line description of E[4] via halving 2-torsion points

ideas.what: Iterating f_2 gives f_{2^n}; the preimage of the origin's image is p(E[2^n])
ideas.modern_name: Lattès map for [2^n]; preimages of the origin give the 2^n-torsion (division-polynomial viewpoint)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but entirely classical computation of the duplication (Lattès) map in a Legendre-type normalization, done relative to a base S. It serves the explicit description of level-4 moduli on the following pages. Nothing here goes beyond standard knowledge.
transcription_corrections: Line 'Pour 0,∞,1 on trouve 1': in the image the list may read '0,∞,t' or '0,∞,1'. Either way, the mathematically correct value at z = 1 is −1.
'on trouve la multiplication [?] f_{2^n}^t' is plausibly 'on trouve les multiplications f_{2^n}^t'.
'par passage au quotient [?]' is plausibly 'par passage au quotient', as transcribed; the handwriting supports it.
The superscript on (f_2^t) appears as '∘n' (n-th iterate); the subscript in f_{2^n}^t overwrites an earlier '2'.
